title: Invalid warning of using `await` on calling @abstract function
body:
### Tested versions

v4.5.stable.mono.official [876b29033]

### System information

Windows 11

### Issue description

Before Godot introduces abstract class/function support, I do my own solution to provide an interface like solution.
The pattern was to have an "interface" class defining all function signatures without an implementation to the user, just an empty function body. 
And have a "hidden" implementation class extending from this interface. 

Now I start to convert my pseudo interfaces to abstract class and see an issue with handling coroutines.
For example, I had an interface function how is a coroutine.
```
	func simulate() -> ClassB:
                # use this line to mark as coroutine
		await get_tree().process_frame
		return self
```
I was able to call the function over the interface using `await a.simulate` without any warnings or errors.
Now after change to abstract I get a warning.  
```
[Ignore]Line 20 (REDUNDANT_AWAIT):"await" keyword is unnecessary because the expression isn't a coroutine nor a signal.
```

`@abstract func simulate() -> ClassB`
I have no option to mark this function as coroutine
      
Sure, I can use `@warning_ignore("redundant_await")` but this could be only a temporary solution.
I provide an API where it is used by third-party users, and it would be annoying to enforce the user to use this fix.



### Steps to reproduce

This code shows the issue.
```
extends RefCounted

# Example of using abstract class
@abstract class ClassA extends Node:
	@abstract func simulate() -> ClassA


class ClassAImpl extends ClassA:
	func simulate() -> ClassA:
		await get_tree().process_frame
		# implement implementaion specific stuff 
		return self


func process_simulate_on_abstract_class_a() -> void:
	var a: ClassA = ClassAImpl.new()

	# This line shows an warining `W 0:00:08:133   GDScript::reload: "await" keyword is unnecessary because the expression isn't a coroutine nor a signal.`
	await a.simulate()



# Example using pseudo interface
class ClassB extends Node:
	func simulate() -> ClassB:
		await get_tree().process_frame
		return self
		

class ClassBImpl extends ClassB:
	func simulate() -> ClassB:
		await get_tree().process_frame
		# implement implementaion specific stuff 
		return self
		
		
func process_simulate_on_abstract_class_b() -> void:
	var b: ClassB = ClassBImpl.new()

	# This line has no warnings
	await b.simulate()
```

n/a
